Hypotheses for the thrombotic microangiopathy: (1) complement‑mediated atypical HUS – supported by low C3, normal C4, renal dominance, and absent severe ADAMTS13 deficiency; (2) secondary TMA from major surgery or occult infection – possible but cultures negative and coagulation normal; (3) TTP – unlikely given ADAMTS13 >10 % and no inhibitor; (4) Shiga‑toxin HUS – no diarrhoea or toxin data; (5) catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome – coagulation studies normal.

Immediate specialist priorities: urgent nephrology and hematology consultation; initiate plasma exchange while awaiting complement results; arrange renal replacement therapy if indicated; send complement gene panel and anti‑factor‑H antibodies; screen for infection, malignancy, and antiphospholipid antibodies; discuss targeted complement inhibition only after confirmatory data. Document all interventions and reassess daily.
